body:
`TileSetAtlasSource::create_alternative_tile` creates an alternative tile for `id = 4097` just fine (with its own TileData):
https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/534591047ee3af8ae828dddd6e206638413f6826/scene/resources/2d/tile_set.cpp#L5384-L5402

However, `TileSetAtlasSource::get_tile_data` removes transform bits (used for the per TileMapLayer cell transformations) from the passed in id:
https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/534591047ee3af8ae828dddd6e206638413f6826/scene/resources/2d/tile_set.cpp#L5459-L5465
https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/534591047ee3af8ae828dddd6e206638413f6826/scene/resources/2d/tile_set.cpp#L5320-L5322
https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/534591047ee3af8ae828dddd6e206638413f6826/scene/resources/2d/tile_set.h#L628-L632

Meaning it ignores 12-th, 13-th and 14-th (counting from 0) bits of the passed in value. That's why it returns TileData for `id = 1` instead of `id = 4097` (as `4096 == 1 << 12`).

---

Besides the above, TileMapCell reserves only 16 bits for alternative tile, but in `TileSetAtlasSource::create_alternative_tile` etc. there are no checks whether the passed id fits into 16 bits.
https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/534591047ee3af8ae828dddd6e206638413f6826/scene/resources/2d/tile_set.h#L60-L66

---

Meanwhile here's a helper method for checking whether the id is valid for TileSetAtlasSource (valid inclusive ranges are: `0..4095`,  `32768..36863`):
```gdscript
static func is_valid_atlas_alternative_id(id: int) -> bool:
	const USABLE_BITS_MASK = 0xFFFF & ~(TileSetAtlasSource.TRANSFORM_FLIP_H | TileSetAtlasSource.TRANSFORM_FLIP_V | TileSetAtlasSource.TRANSFORM_TRANSPOSE)
	return id == (id & USABLE_BITS_MASK)
```
(No idea why transform flags were assigned `1 << 12`, `1 << 13`, `1 << 14` instead of the last 3 available bits (`1 << 13`, ` 1 << 14`, `1 << 15`). But changing it now would be compatibility breaking and hence is not feasible.)

I'm having issues with my scene tiles after testing upgrading to 4.6 beta 2. 
My project saves a custom resource that includes PackedScenes. When the user loads the project, the resource is loaded in, and the scenes are added to the relevant tilesets using the id associated with each "game_object" the scene belongs to, as the id for the scene tile. I'm not getting any errors during that process.

When the game later tries to place a tile, I run this code:
```
if tile_set.get_source(0).has_scene_tile_id(id):
		set_cell(coordinates, 0, Vector2i(0, 0), id)
	else:
		print("Failed to find object tile with id: ", id)
```
I'm seeing a lot of missing tiles, and every one of them that's missing has an id higher than 4096. Almost all of the tiles it does place are also the incorrect scene. 

Given that, if I understand correctly, scene tiles are added as alternative tiles, it seems like this could be the issue I'm having.
This is the same scene in 4.5.1 stable, vs 4.6 beta 2

> Given that, if I understand correctly, scene tiles are added as alternative tiles, it seems like this could be the issue I'm having. @TanyaPegasus Indeed this seems to be the issue you're having. > When the game later tries to place a tile, I run this code: > > ``` > if tile_set.get_source(0).has_scene_tile_id(id): > set_cell(coordinates, 0, Vector2i(0, 0), id) > else: > print("Failed to find object tile with id: ", id) > ``` Note that even if `TileSetScenesCollectionSource::has_scene_tile_id(id)` returns true, setting such `id` for a TileMapLayer cell with `TileMapLayer::set_cell(..., id)` might still silently fail / truncate the `id` to 16 bits (as I've hinted in my previous comment). Note it's using `int16_t` type which is signed, meaning TileMapLayer is capable of storing ids in range `-32768 ... 32767`. But [`TileSetScenesCollectionSource` prevents any negative ids](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/63227bbc8ae5300319f14f8253c8158b846f355b/scene/resources/2d/tile_set.cpp#L5780-L5812), meaning the sign bit (`1 << 15`) is pretty much wasted / used only for indicating invalid tile (`TileSetSource::INVALID_TILE_ALTERNATIVE == -1`). So with the transform bits introduced in `4.6` for the scene tiles (#108010), valid usable ids in `TileSetScenesCollectionSource` that are actually usable in `TileMapLayer` are only `0 ... 4095` (in `4.5` it's `0 ... 32767`).
Test script

```gdscript @tool extends EditorScript func _run() -> void: print(Engine.get_version_info().string) var id_from := -(1 << 17) var id_to := (1 << 17) - 1 print("Checking id range (inclusive): %7d ... %-7d" % [id_from, id_to]) print() print("TileSetScenesCollectionSource.create_scene_tile(..., id) -> TileSetScenesCollectionSource.has_scene_tile(id)") test_scenes_source_has_scene_tile_id(id_from, id_to) print() print("TileSetScenesCollectionSource.create_scene_tile(..., id) -> TileMapLayer.set_cell(..., id) -> TileMapLayer.get_cell_alternative_tile() == id") test_tile_map_layer_set_cell_scene_tile_id(id_from, id_to) func test_scenes_source_has_scene_tile_id(id_from: int, id_to : int) -> void: var t1 := Time.get_ticks_usec() var in_range := false var in_valid_range := false var range_start: int var range_end: int for id in range(id_from, id_to + 1): var scenes_source := TileSetScenesCollectionSource.new() scenes_source.create_scene_tile(null, id) var tile_set := TileSet.new() tile_set.add_source(scenes_source, 0) var has_tile := scenes_source.has_scene_tile_id(id) if not in_range or in_valid_range != has_tile: if in_range: print("%-7s: %7d ... %-7d" % [ "Valid" if in_valid_range else "Invalid", range_start, range_end ]) in_range = true range_start = id in_valid_range = has_tile range_end = id if in_range: print("%-7s: %7d ... %-7d" % [ "Valid" if in_valid_range else "Invalid", range_start, range_end ]) var t2 := Time.get_ticks_usec() print("Took: %d usec" % [t2 - t1]) func test_tile_map_layer_set_cell_scene_tile_id(id_from: int, id_to : int) -> void: var t1 := Time.get_ticks_usec() var in_range := false var in_valid_range := false var range_start: int var range_end: int for id in range(id_from, id_to + 1): var scenes_source := TileSetScenesCollectionSource.new() scenes_source.create_scene_tile(null, id) var tile_set := TileSet.new() var source_id := 0 tile_set.add_source(scenes_source, source_id) var layer := TileMapLayer.new() layer.tile_set = tile_set var cell_coords := Vector2i(1, 2) layer.set_cell(cell_coords, source_id, Vector2i(0, 0), id) var correct_tile_id := layer.get_cell_alternative_tile(cell_coords) == id layer.free() if not in_range or in_valid_range != correct_tile_id: if in_range: print("%-7s: %7d ... %-7d" % [ "Valid" if in_valid_range else "Invalid", range_start, range_end ]) in_range = true range_start = id in_valid_range = correct_tile_id range_end = id if in_range: print("%-7s: %7d ... %-7d" % [ "Valid" if in_valid_range else "Invalid", range_start, range_end ]) var t2 := Time.get_ticks_usec() print("Took: %d usec" % [t2 - t1]) ```

Outputs: ``` 4.5.1-stable (official) Checking id range (inclusive): -131072 ... 131071 TileSetScenesCollectionSource.create_scene_tile(..., id) -> TileSetScenesCollectionSource.has_scene_tile(id) Invalid: -131072 ... -1 Valid : 0 ... 131071 Took: 886653 usec TileSetScenesCollectionSource.create_scene_tile(..., id) -> TileMapLayer.set_cell(..., id) -> TileMapLayer.get_cell_alternative_tile() == id Invalid: -131072 ... -32769 Valid : -32768 ... 32767 Invalid: 32768 ... 131071 Took: 1922803 usec ``` ``` 4.6-beta2 (official) Checking id range (inclusive): -131072 ... 131071 TileSetScenesCollectionSource.create_scene_tile(..., id) -> TileSetScenesCollectionSource.has_scene_tile(id) Invalid: -131072 ... -1 Valid : 0 ... 4095 Invalid: 4096 ... 32767 Valid : 32768 ... 36863 Invalid: 36864 ... 65535 Valid : 65536 ... 69631 Invalid: 69632 ... 98303 Valid : 98304 ... 102399 Invalid: 102400 ... 131071 Took: 918501 usec TileSetScenesCollectionSource.create_scene_tile(..., id) -> TileMapLayer.set_cell(..., id) -> TileMapLayer.get_cell_alternative_tile() == id Invalid: -131072 ... -32769 Valid : -32768 ... 32767 Invalid: 32768 ... 131071 Took: 1800965 usec ``` > I'm having issues with my scene tiles after testing upgrading to 4.6 beta 2. My project saves a custom resource that includes PackedScenes. When the user loads the project, the resource is loaded in, and the scenes are added to the relevant tilesets using the id associated with each "game_object" the scene belongs to, as the id for the scene tile. I'm not getting any errors during that process. Not sure what exactly you're using as _the id associated with each "game_object"_ but as mentioned you can safely use ids in range: - `0 ... 32767` in `4.5`, - `0 ... 4095` in `4.6`. So _(in the current state)_ in case you need more then 4096 scene tiles in the TileSet, you'd need to create another TileSetScenesCollectionSource. --- cc @groud This could be considered compatibility breaking. Possible approaches I see: - We consider current state "just fine" as 4096 scene tiles per source is not awful and compatibility breaking is worth the feature (scene tile transforms). - Revert #108010, forget scene tiles rotations/flips/transposing. - Try utilizing more bits for scene tile ids. Since scene tiles atlas coords need to be set to `(0, 0)`, we could possibly allow only 2 values per atlas coord: `-1` and `0`. This would allow to store atlas coords for the scene tiles in 2 bits only, leaving the remaining `32 - 2 = 30` bits of `TileMapCell::coord_x` and `TileMapCell::coord_y` free to use for the id. :thinking: https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/63227bbc8ae5300319f14f8253c8158b846f355b/scene/resources/2d/tile_set.h#L60-L68

Clarifying what I mean by "Id's associated with each game_object":
My project is a planner for another game. The main game can output a map of what the real current state is, and players can then test placements before building in the actual game. What this means is that all the scenes I'm using are things from that game, which it calls "objects", and which I call "game_object", just to make things a bit clearer (differentiating from an OOP Object).
In the main game, each "object" has an id associated with it. While not ideal, those id's are sequential numbers. When I add my scenes to the source, I override the id to match the id the main game would have set for the scene. The id's currently go up to about 17.6k. While there are gaps caused by things like objects that were later deleted, there are still about 10.2k actual objects I need to add. 

For me, this update is definitely compatibility breaking. I could split those scenes amongst several layers (and already do somewhat, to differentiate between the smaller set of floors, and the bulk of the objects which are other items), doing so would cause even more complexity for me. The objects can overlap as you can probably see in the image above, and they should do that in a very particular way, to match the way the main game handles layering sprites. If all of mine aren't on the same layer, then I need to do a lot more to make that happen. I also can't change the numbering system of the original game, so would have to account for a lot of change in my program to track what source id matches each game id, to then place the correct scenes.

The other thing I would point out is that Godot exposes the source id's to be changed by the user in 2 separate places that I can see. Inside create_scene_tile(), as well as set_scene_tile_id(). I believe that this means that even if most people don't have as many scenes as me, I'm unlikely to be the only person who has some custom system of id's, which is not guaranteed to stay under 4096. In the scheme of things, that really isn't that large of a number. I'm unlikely to be the only person to have a project broken by this change. 

I suggest that even if this change isn't reverted, it's vital that those two functions mentioned above prevent you from using invalid id's, and that the documentation clearly state the maximum. Having it all just break randomly with no warning is very confusing.

> We consider current state "just fine" as 4096 scene tiles per source is not awful and compatibility breaking is worth the feature (scene tile transforms).

I think we should go that way. 4096 scene tiles are probably more that enough for 99.9% use cases.

Now, maybe a solution might be to move the scene ID to the atlas_coords field in the TileMap data. Not sure how we could keep compatibility though. Maybe by copying the field over from the alternative_tile field to the atlas_coords one, if atlas_coords is zero and alternative_tile is not ? That could maybe work.

Edit: though thinking about it, the issue is that TileMap is not aware of what kind of sources it stores if it does not have an assigned TileSet.

> I suggest that even if this change isn't reverted, it's vital that those two functions mentioned above prevent you from using invalid id's, and that the documentation clearly state the maximum. Having it all just break randomly with no warning is very confusing.

Yeah I agree with that, functions should check for boundaries.

@TanyaPegasus Thanks for the clarification!

> While not ideal, those id's are sequential numbers.

I'd say that's good as it allows to easily chunk them.

> For me, this update is definitely compatibility breaking. I could split those scenes amongst several layers (and already do somewhat, to differentiate between the smaller set of floors, and the bulk of the objects which are other items), doing so would cause even more complexity for me. The objects can overlap as you can probably see in the image above, and they should do that in a very particular way, to match the way the main game handles layering sprites. If all of mine aren't on the same layer, then I need to do a lot more to make that happen. I also can't change the numbering system of the original game, so would have to account for a lot of change in my program to track what source id matches each game id, to then place the correct scenes.

The thing is you don't need to split those scenes amongst several layers. You can split your single all-scene-tiles-TileSetScenesCollectionSource into multiple chunk-TileSetScenesCollectionSource, all within the same TileSet (you could of course still use such TileSet in different layers if needed). Something like (example for your 17.6k objects):

game_object_id|source_id|alternative_id
-|-|-
0 ... 4095|chunk0_source_id|0 ... 4095
4096 ... 8191|chunk1_source_id|0 ... 4095
8192 ... 12287|chunk2_source_id|0 ... 4095
12288 ... 16383|chunk3_source_id|0 ... 4095
16384 ... 17599|chunk4_source_id|0 ... 1215

Here's a snippet presenting the idea (not tested anyhow):
```gdscript
var tile_set: TileSet = ...

var scene_tile_chunk_index_to_source_id: Dictionary[int, int]
const SCENE_TILES_PER_SOURCE: int = 4096
const SCENE_SOURCE_INVALID_ID: int = -1


func create_scene_tile(scene: PackedScene, game_object_id: int) -> void:
	var chunk_index: int = game_object_id / SCENE_TILES_PER_SOURCE
	var chunk_source_id: int = scene_tile_chunk_index_to_source_id.get(chunk_index, SCENE_SOURCE_INVALID_ID)

	var chunk_source: TileSetScenesCollectionSource
	if chunk_source_id != SCENE_SOURCE_INVALID_ID:
		chunk_source = tile_set.get_source(chunk_source_id)
	else:
		chunk_source = TileSetScenesCollectionSource.new()
		chunk_source_id = tile_set.add_source(chunk_source)
		chunk_index_to_source_id[chunk_index] = chunk_source_id
		
	var alternative_id: int = game_object_id % SCENE_TILES_PER_SOURCE
	var created_alternative_id: int = chunk_source.create_scene_tile(scene, alternative_id)
	assert(alternative_id == created_alternative_id)


func game_object_id_to_tile_source_id(game_object_id: int) -> int:
	var chunk_index: int = game_object_id / SCENE_TILES_PER_SOURCE
	return scene_tile_chunk_index_to_source_id.get(chunk_index, SCENE_SOURCE_INVALID_ID)

func game_object_id_to_tile_alternative_id(game_object_id: int) -> int:
	return game_object_id % SCENE_TILES_PER_SOURCE
```

Then instead of doing something like:
```gdscript
layer.set_cell(cell_coords, all_scene_tiles_source_id, Vector2i(0, 0), game_object_id)
```
you'd do:
```gdscript
var source_id: int = game_object_id_to_tile_source_id(game_object_id)
var alternative_id: int = game_object_id_to_tile_alternative_id(game_object_id)
layer.set_cell(cell_coords, source_id, Vector2i(0, 0), alternative_id)
```

All I'm saying here is that is not very hard to account for that limit.

> I suggest that even if this change isn't reverted, it's vital that those two functions mentioned above prevent you from using invalid id's, and that the documentation clearly state the maximum. Having it all just break randomly with no warning is very confusing.

Absolutely! I think we all agree this needs to be documented and communicated to the user when exceeding the allowed limit (whatever the limit is). But before doing so we need to decide whether we want to change the current state somehow. After documenting the limits, such limits would be pretty much set in stone (if the limit in 4.5 was documented then I think we wouldn't be able to consider changing the limit to be "just fine").

---

> Now, maybe a solution might be to move the scene ID to the atlas_coords field in the TileMap data. Not sure how we could keep compatibility though. Maybe by copying the field over from the alternative_tile field to the atlas_coords one, if atlas_coords is zero and alternative_tile is not ? That could maybe work.
> 
> Edit: though thinking about it, the issue is that TileMap is not aware of what kind of sources it stores if it does not have an assigned TileSet.

Ah right, TileMapLayer doesn't care about the source, [it just returns relevant CellData field for the given cell](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/63227bbc8ae5300319f14f8253c8158b846f355b/scene/2d/tile_map_layer.cpp#L2849-L2880). So making these return different data depending on the source it refers to would introduce more inconsistency / potential confusion I think. So I'm dismissing that idea.

Another possibility is to actually use the sign bit of the `TileMapCell::alternative_id`. But this would only raise to limit to 8191 usable ids (`4096 * 2 - 1` for the invalid id indicator (`-1`)). So this would still not help with [the issue mentioned here (17.6k ids)](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/112175#issuecomment-3684808907). Also this would not be so straighforward to do, so I think it's not worth the effort/complicating things.

This leaves 2 options: either leave it as is, or revert #108010.

> I think we should go that way. 4096 scene tiles are probably more that enough for 99.9% use cases.

I agree, I also suspect it being quite unusual. Besides, I think I presented above that manually making some kind of chunk system (in case more than 4096 scene tiles are needed) is not that hard. Also what's important, the previous limit was not documented so breaking it with introducing scene tile transformations is not that bad.

Thank you for the response. I appreciate the time you took to write that out for me.

After making my post yesterday, I thought a lot about it. I had taken a break from my project, and was a bit rusty on how some of it worked. I realised later that you meant multiple sources in the same TileSet, on the same layer, which makes sense.

As someone at the part of their coding journey where I know there are good ways to do things, and I want to do them the best way I can, but don't always know what that best way is, it makes me feel really good that the method I came up with is similar to what you've suggested to me.

I have a custom resource called game_object. It has a lot of fields about the game objects that the main game specifies. The main game uses .txt files to store a lot of information, so I read those into Godot and convert them into something more usable. Instead of adding even more fields to that, I was thinking maybe a calculate_source_id(), and a calculate_scene_id() function. The first returns `int(id / MAX_SCENE_TILE_ID)`, and the second returns `id % MAX_SCENE_TILE_ID`.
I genuinely wasn't sure which is the better of the two, adding the new fields and therefore storing more data (2 more numbers for about 10.2k total objects), or performing those calculations whenever the info is needed. Would love to hear the opinion of someone more experienced.

I would say that after having had a couple of days to take in finding my completely broken project, think on it, and realise the solution isn't as complicated as I thought it might be, I don't think this is as big of an issue as I first did. 4095 is certainly not as flexible of a number, but it seems there are viable workarounds. I don't think I ever saw a limit mentioned in the past. I just think people wouldn't have been as surprised if they hit that 8 x higher limit that was there before. It seems that if there isn't another option, the new functionality is worth the limit it imposes.

When I was testing the beta version, the first thing I did was look at the blog post. I saw the breaking changes section, which leads you to github, clicked on that, and skimmed everything there to see if anything sounded relevant to me. After having opened my project and having found most of my tiles missing and the rest incorrect and often upside down, that tag could be helpful to add to this. Fixing it so that it correctly imposes the limit when setting the id, and warns you about why would make it less of a surprise though.

One final thought is, for me, I was adding my tiles to the source via code, and didn't get a warning when doing so. The way I have things set up to allow for updates to the main game, means I'm adding my tiles to the set at run time. For anyone who may have already added oddly numbered scenes to their sets, they're not going to get a warning from those functions, because they won't be using them again. Godot will need to detect a SceneCollectionSource with too many ids in it, and tell them about it. That could still be an issue if they have high, overridden ids, but less than 4096 total scenes, because as far as Godot is concerned they're valid numbers with transforms applied. So would definitely be good to make it easy to find this when they go searching for the bug.

They will get a spam of errors (after proper errors are added) as relevant methods are being called during loading/setting the properties:
